title: Runtime Version Evolution Policy — safe schema changes, deprecation cadence, and rollout gates
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Purpose: define a pragmatic, operationally-safe semantic versioning and LTS policy for the serving runtime. Scope: breaking-change rules, deprecation cadence, compatibility guarantees, LTS channel criteria, rollout gates, and supporting tooling for upgrade checks and migrations. This policy is intended for release engineers, runtime maintainers, SDK teams, and platform customers running Dedicated/Private deployments.

Goals: 1) Minimize surprise outages from incompatible upgrades. 2) Provide clear, automatable gates for safe rollout. 3) Make deprecations discoverable and easy to migrate away from. 4) Support backports for LTS releases with well-defined patch rules.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical semver interpretation document for the runtime that all teams agree on
A short checklist (pre-release) that gates every runtime release: API-compatibility-smoke, migration-tests, changelog entry, and docs updates
Automated CI check that fails PRs introducing public surface-breaking changes unless the PR includes a deprecation plan
An LTS branching rule and backport matrix published in the release playbook
Rollout gate definitions implemented in release pipelines (canary steps, metrics thresholds)
policy_summary: Semver baseline: runtime follows MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH semantics for public HTTP/SDK/in-process APIs exposed in the contract directory

MAJOR: incompatible API changes that require migration. Allowed only with a migration guide, feature flag, and explicit opt-in timeline. Must be scheduled as a major release or as a non-default runtime variant.
MINOR: additive changes and opt-in features. Backwards-compatible enhancements. Minor releases may include deprecations but must not remove behavior without a prior deprecation cycle.
PATCH: bug fixes, non-API behavioral fixes, security patches. Must not change public contracts or introduce deprecations.
Deprecation windows: default 3 release cycles (approx 90 days) for API surface on hosted; 180 days for Dedicated/Private customers with labeled migration assistance unless explicitly negotiated.

Compatibility classification: public API surfaces are classified as stable, experimental, or internal. Only stable surfaces are subject to semver guarantees. Experimental may change between minors without deprecation but must be marked and documented. Internal surfaces can change without notice.

LTS channel: an LTS candidate is a minor release that meets stability and coverage criteria (no regressions for 3 consecutive weeks, passing stress tests). LTS is maintained for at least 12 months with patch-backports only. LTS backports follow strict risk assessment.
Backport rules: security and critical reliability fixes are eligible. New features are not backported. All backports require automated regressions and owner sign-off.
rollout_gates: Preflight: API compatibility smoke tests across major client SDKs and the compatibility matrix generator must pass
Canary: staged rollout to 1% of traffic for 24 hours with rolling monitoring of error rate, p50/p95 latency, and unit-cost metrics
Intermediate ramp: 10% for 48 hours if canary metrics stable; automated comparison to baseline using error budget thresholds
Full rollout: proceed after 72 hours of stable intermediate ramp and no customer-impact alerts
Abort criteria: +30% increase in error rate vs baseline, or p95 latency regression >30%, or any SLO breach tied to core generation endpoints
upgrade_tooling_requirements: runtime-upgrade-check CLI: checks customer projects against a compatibility matrix and flags deprecated API usage
migration-guides generator: templates per deprecated API with code snippets across supported SDKs
ci-gate job that runs 'compat-smoke' on PRs touching contract files and fails when breaking changes are detected without deprecation metadata
changelog linting: releases must include structured CHANGELOG entries with "breaking_changes", "deprecations", and "migration_notes" sections
binary/runtime feature flags support for gradual enablement and optional opt-in major-version variants
documentation_and_communication: Release playbook page in Confluence with the LTS matrix, example rollout timelines, and emergency rollback runbook
Automated release notes posted to /releases and included in the Console 'release' dashboard
Dedicated migration email and changelog digest for Dedicated/Private customers when deprecations are announced
SDK teams must add deprecation warnings in client libraries and surface compile-time or runtime alerts where feasible
rollback_plan: If canary/intermediate gates trigger abort criteria, immediate rollback to previous runtime variant via the release pipeline. For Dedicated/Private customers, trigger coordinated rollback with SE and support; log and capture heap and traces for diagnosis. All rollbacks must create a postmortem ticket within 48 hours describing root cause and remediation steps.
monitoring_and_telemetry: SLOs to monitor: request success rate, p95 latency (generation), token throughput, and unit-cost per 1k tokens
Custom compatibility metrics: number of deprecated API hits per hour, migration progress across customers
Alerting thresholds tied to rollout gates and integrated with oncall rotation
implementation_steps: Draft canonical semver guidance doc and circulate for review (owners: runtime-team, sdk-team)
Implement compat-smoke CI job and integrate with PR workflow
Add structured changelog requirement to release checklist and release tooling
Build runtime-upgrade-check CLI prototype and run against 2 major enterprise customer configs
Define LTS eligibility automation and publish LTS schedule in release playbook
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: customers on heavy custom integrations may be broken by minor/major changes — Mitigation: early customer communication, migration assistance, opt-in feature flags
Risk: incomplete detection of public surface changes — Mitigation: contract-driven tests, codeowners for contract files, PR automation
Risk: backport churn on LTS — Mitigation: strict eligibility and risk assessment, prioritize automated test coverage
